WHAT THIS MODEL DEMANDS THAT THE CURRENT FLEET DOES NOT SUPPLY.

**0. REAL EGRESS. THE BLUNTEST DEMAND.** Three of the five W0 registries state up front that the egress proxy blocked nearly every .gov and .mil host, so their endpoint grammars, parameter names and identifier schemes were reconstructed from search snippets and prior knowledge. This model is built entirely on resolve-or-die. Without working egress to cia.gov, apps.dtic.mil, catalog.archives.gov, govinfo.gov, comptroller.war.gov, prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com, county recorders and the rest, every receipt fails, every candidate is V0, and the entire register grades F. The verification tier is not a nice-to-have that degrades gracefully — it is the load-bearing member. Before W1 runs: verify egress per host, fetch every robots.txt, and re-verify each endpoint grammar in the registries against the live target.

**1. A VERIFIER TIER BETWEEN DISCOVERY AND ADJUDICATION — DETERMINISTIC, NOT AN LLM.** No agent in the current fleet resolves a citation to bytes. ARCHIVIST finds, LINEAGE traces, REFUTER argues, ASSESSOR scores; nobody fetches. VERIFIER must be code, not a model: fetch, hash, store, and confirm a quoted span at character offsets by string comparison. Where a model is unavoidable, it must be a different family from the discoverer. An LLM verifying an LLM shares the priors that produced the error.

**2. IDENTIFIER GRAMMAR VALIDATORS AND RESOLVERS FOR ~15 CLASSES.** CREST CIA-RDP, DTIC AD (including ADB-prefix detection, which is a positive KNOWN-TO-EXIST-NOT-RELEASED state and a ready-made FOIA worklist), NARA NAID, GAO report numbers, Federal Register cites, GovInfo package IDs, FCC ASR registrations, FPDS PIIDs, FRUS volume/document pairs, USGS quad name+year, county parcel IDs, MSHA MINE_IDs, AFHRA IRIS numbers, DOIs, IA identifiers. Three checks in order: grammar, resolution, **metadata match**. The registries' own instruction — 'Do not construct identifiers; enumerate them' — is a bare admission that identifier confabulation is the expected agent behaviour, and it must become a schema constraint rather than a note.

**3. AN AGENT THAT PRODUCES NEGATIVE RECEIPTS.** Call it SILENCE. Nothing in the current fleet records a search that found nothing. This model cannot function without it: the ERP machinery, the X band, the ORIGIN dispositive definition and refutation R3 all consume logged negative searches with query string, corpus, corpus version, executed_at and result count. **Absence is not citable without a receipt for the absence.** This is also the only honest way to distinguish 'we looked and found nothing' from 'we did not look' — the distinction v0.1 could not draw and which is half of what the register is for.

**4. A PROPOSITION DECOMPOSER (PROPOSER).** Before anything is scored, a candidate must be decomposed into the closed eleven-class vocabulary with subjects, predicate arguments and as-of dates. No such agent exists. Without it, agents will keep emitting site-level dossiers and the unit error returns through the back door.

**5. A NULL PROPOSER, AND REFUTER PROMOTED TO CO-SCORER.** `null_hypothesis` is not nullable. REFUTER must instantiate the enumerated alternative set per proposition — {commercial or industrial mine or quarry, highway or rail tunnel, water or sewer works, subway or utility vault, agricultural or cold storage, data centre, already-registered decommissioned silo, mine reclamation, ordinary large building of its class, nothing at all} — disposition each, and publish the table. REFUTER currently has no numeric hook; here it owns two of five band conditions plus an override, and its prior becomes typology-conditional rather than blanket-refute.

**6. LINEAGE REBUILT ON SEMANTIC CLUSTERING.** The registries specify MinHash shingling against the mirrored aggregator corpus. That detects copying; the dominant mechanism is now regeneration, which shares no strings and cites nothing. LINEAGE needs claim-level semantic clustering with first-observation dating as tiebreaker, Wayback CDX `collapse=digest` for change-history rather than capture-lists, and the counterfactual test administered by quorum across model families with disagreement logged. Same-model collapse must be enforced in the schema, not in LINEAGE's judgement.

**7. A CURATOR AND THREE REVIEWED-WRITE TABLES.** Tier (158 rows, one ladder), diagnosticity catalog (per typology), and expected-record profile. These must be foreign keys. An agent may PROPOSE a row; the assignment is a reviewed write. Three incompatible tier ladders already exist in W0 output before a single candidate has been graded — at continuous unbounded ingest, tier assignment is not a stable variable unless it stops being a judgement.

**8. A CANARY PROGRAMME.** Rotating fabricated facility names with zero corpus presence injected into the discovery queue every cycle. Any citation returned is a directly measured hallucination against known ground truth. Paired with the format-valid-but-unresolvable rate and per-agent grade distributions, this converts the largest unquantified risk in the project into a monitored, published number.

**9. CROSS-FAMILY DOUBLE-SCORING.** A rolling 10% sample re-scored blind by a different model family, with per-condition agreement published. High inter-family agreement on VERIFIED sources is corroboration; high agreement on UNVERIFIED assertions is a shared-prior signature and must raise suspicion, not confidence.

**10. AN ECHO GUARD.** The register must keep a complete timestamped log of everything it has published, quarantine post-publication sources, and emit a machine-readable provenance beacon on every entry and API response. Nothing in the current design knows what the register has said, which means nothing can stop it re-ingesting its own output as corroboration.

**11. AN INJECTION-SAFE INGESTION PATH.** The string 'prompt inject' appears zero times across all 353KB of W0 output, while the geospatial registry specifies sweeping Wikimapia by bounding box with the military category filter — a documented ingestion path into an adversary-writable free-text field. Required: fetched text as data behind a hard structural boundary; identifiers from untrusted text as leads; cache-and-revalidate with content hashes and drift alerts replacing 'hit them once'; an adversary-writable flag per source, surfaced on the entry page; and an injection red-team suite in CI against the live path.

**12. RESOLVER REWRITTEN.** Its current brief — 'merge name variants, alias chains, coordinate near-duplicates' — describes the correct Kirtland merge (KUMMSC/KUMSC) and the catastrophic one (Manzano Base/KUMMSC) in identical language. It needs: an IDENTITY proposition as a merge precondition, non-pooling evidence, a split operation, entity_level, and a DISTINCT-FROM relation seeded from the calibration set.

**13. NULL RETURNS FROM TIER 1.** Every discovery agent must report sites examined and rejected, with reasons. Nothing currently rewards an agent for saying 'I looked and there is nothing here', while the COMPLETENESS CRITIC explicitly pushes toward filling map gaps — which, in a find-rewarded fleet, manufactures candidates in sparse regions.

**14. THE FLEET MUST BE ABLE TO SAY X.** Nothing in the current design has any way to emit 'not assessed', and every incentive runs the other way. X will be the modal grade for a long time, and a register that is honestly mostly-X is more credible than one that is dishonestly mostly-C. This needs to be stated in the agent briefs, rewarded in the telemetry, and rendered distinctly in the interface.

**15. SCORER PINNING AND VERSION DISCIPLINE.** Every grade row records the scoring model ID, rubric version, and all three table versions. No grade is comparable across versions without re-scoring the baseline. The confidence-history chart — the project's flagship honesty artifact — must suppress SCORER-CHANGE, TABLE-VERSION-CHANGE and RESCORE-NOISE entirely, or it will publish model drift as an evidence narrative with a fluent justification attached.

**16. AND ONE THING THE FLEET GETS FOR FREE.** Blind fan-out is retained, but its justification changes from corroboration to RECALL. Seven agents on seven beats over one indexed web is a good recall strategy and contributes exactly nothing to independence. That sentence should be in the agent briefs, because the opposite sentence is currently in §2 and will be quoted at the project.
tradeoffs:
HONEST WEAKNESSES, AND WHAT THIS MODEL STILL CANNOT EXPRESS.

**1. IT IS BRITTLE AT BAND BOUNDARIES, AND DELIBERATELY SO.** A proposition one condition short of B sits at C indefinitely. There is no partial credit, no 'nearly B', no way to say a candidate is 0.9 of the way there. Greenbrier-1991 is B or C depending on whether a SECOND construction worker is independently resolvable — a single binary fact swings a band. The mitigation is transparency rather than smoothing: `limiting_condition` names the exact criterion, so a reader sees the hinge and a researcher knows precisely what to go find. But this is a real cost, and users accustomed to scores will experience it as arbitrariness. I judge the trade worth it, because a continuous score that moves smoothly is also a score that moves on noise.

**2. IT REFUSES TO OUTPUT A PROBABILITY, AND PEOPLE WILL READ ONE ANYWAY.** The historian asked for P(EXISTS) as a published number. This model declines. It publishes grade + ceiling + at_ceiling + silence_reading, which is *more* information but is not a probability, cannot be aggregated, cannot be plotted, and cannot be compared across propositions. 'EXIST B, at ceiling, silence uninformative' is the honest statement and it is genuinely harder to read than '0.85'. Readers will convert the letters back into numbers in their heads, and the ceiling and silence fields will be the first things dropped when someone quotes the register. A register that is quoted lossily is a real failure mode and I have no defence against it beyond design.

**3. THE THREE TABLES ARE ASSERTED, NOT DERIVED — AND THEY ARE THE NEW ATTACK SURFACE.** The tier table, the diagnosticity catalog and the ERP profiles carry all the judgement that v0.1 put in the weight vector. I have moved judgement from per-candidate scoring (where it is unreproducible) into versioned lookups (where it is auditable and back-fittable), which is a large improvement — but it is a relocation, not an elimination. The diagnosticity anchors in particular are my estimates informed by two prior lenses; they have not been back-fitted against outcomes because there are no outcomes yet. The ERP table encodes a policy about how American secrecy works that could simply be wrong for some agency or era, and being wrong there is invisible: it silently licenses or forbids the argument from silence. These tables need re-derivation after the first 25 adjudications and periodically thereafter, and their version IDs must be on every grade row so a bad table version can be identified and rolled back.

**4. IT CANNOT RANK WITHIN A BAND.** Two C-grade propositions are not comparable, and there is no defensible way to sort a list. For a register whose interface is a map, this matters: 'show me the strongest candidates in Virginia' has no well-defined answer beyond band membership. Sorting by band then by lineage count is available but is not a claim the model endorses.

**5. IT CANNOT EXPRESS DEGREE.** HARDEN is a proposition, not a quantity. 'Designed against a 200–300 MT surface burst' and 'has a heavy door' both reach A if the documents support them, and the model has no way to say one is a hundred times the other. The same flattening applies to depth, capacity, and extent. Predicate arguments carry some of this as text, but the grade does not.

**6. THE LINEAGE COUNTERFACTUAL REMAINS A JUDGEMENT CALL, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING.** Rule 7 — 'would this source have produced this claim if the prior source had never existed?' — decides CAP-1 and B1, which is the difference between C and B on a great many entries. I have quorum-adjudicated it across model families and required logging, but I have not made it mechanical, and I do not think it can be made mechanical. Hard cases are genuinely hard: two Greenbrier construction workers on the same job, in the same town, over thirty years, are somewhere between one witness and two, and the model forces a binary.

**7. X WILL DOMINATE, AND AN X-HEAVY REGISTER LOOKS EMPTY.** The canonical search sets are long, verification is slow, and the honest default for a newly ingested candidate is X. For a considerable period the register will be mostly 'not assessed', which is truthful, unusual, and commercially unappealing. There is a real temptation, under pressure to look substantial, to weaken the canonical-coverage requirement. That temptation is the most likely way this model gets quietly abandoned in practice, and it will not announce itself as an abandonment.

**8. RESOLVE-OR-DIE IMPORTS A NEW BIAS: TOWARD THE ONLINE.** A document held only in paper at College Park cannot produce a receipt. NARA's textual holdings are ~96% undigitised, and RG 77, RG 374 and RG 397 — where the construction record actually lives — are overwhelmingly paper. RG 373 domestic aerial photography is entirely manual, three-day retrieval from Lenexa, no remote access path. Pre-1994 congressional material is scanned-only and unevenly digitised, and the fuller record sits behind ProQuest's paywall. So the model systematically favours what has been digitised over what is merely true, which is a *different* bias from v0.1's favouring of the disclosed, but a bias nonetheless. Partial mitigation: an intermediate state 'series-level description exists, contents unexamined' feeding a documented ARCHIVE-GAP flag, plus the coverage map. It does not close the hole; digitisation and physical research trips do.

**9. THE PRE-2022 WATERLINE (CAP-4) WILL PRODUCE FALSE NEGATIVES AND WILL AGE BADLY.** Genuinely new, genuinely human reporting published after November 2022 with a thin byline history is capped at D alongside content-farm regeneration. That is unfair to real journalism and real researchers, and the unfairness compounds every year the waterline stays fixed. It is a blunt instrument justified only by the absence of a better one, and it should be revisited as attribution infrastructure improves.

**10. R2 (NULL DOMINANT) CAN BE TOO SEVERE.** The DIA disagreement with the IC lens is the visible instance: R2 fires whenever a documented mundane explanation accounts for everything, which is correct for SubTropolis and DIA but could refute a genuine dual-use facility whose cover story is *also* completely true and completely documented — which is precisely what a good cover story is. Greenbrier's Forsythe Associates arrangement is the cautionary case: had the cover been slightly more documented, R2 might have fired on a real COG facility in 1991. The 'no D3+ residual' condition is the only thing standing between the model and that error, and it depends entirely on the diagnosticity catalog being right about what counts as D3.

**11. NOTHING HERE HELPS WITH A GENUINELY NOVEL TYPOLOGY.** The diagnosticity catalog is a closed table with a D0 default. A facility type nobody has catalogued — a new construction method, a new concealment pattern, a class of site that does not resemble anything in the registries — produces observations that all default to D0 and grades D forever. The model is conservative by construction and will be slowest exactly where it would be most valuable. Catalog extension is a reviewed write and therefore a bottleneck.

**12. IT DOES NOT SOLVE FOREIGN AND NON-ENGLISH MATERIAL.** Receipts, identifier grammars, ERP profiles and canonical search sets are all US-specific. The schema is country-agnostic, but every table in Part 5 and Part 6 would need rebuilding per country, and the FOREIGN agent's beat currently has no verification path at all. US-first is the ratified decision, but the model is more US-shaped than the schema admits.

**13. AND THE ONE IT CANNOT ARGUE ITS WAY OUT OF: THIS SPECIFICATION IS ITSELF UNVERIFIED.** It was written by reading five registries, three of which state that their endpoint grammars and identifier schemes were reconstructed from memory and search snippets because .gov egress was blocked. I have not resolved a single CREST identifier, fetched a single HTMC sheet, or confirmed that `historicaltopo.csv` has the columns the registry says it has. The diagnosticity anchors, the ERP defaults and the canonical search sets are all downstream of that. By this model's own standard, this document is V0-UNRESOLVED: format-valid, internally consistent, and unverified. It should be treated as a specification to be checked, not a finding — and the first task after ratification is to run its own tables through its own verification tier.
